If you had a baby in 2025 or 2026, the federal government has $1,000 waiting for your child in a new Trump account. But automatically enrolled does not mean automatically paid.

Jake FitzGerald of 24/7 Wall St. walks through the two separate steps families keep merging into one. First, claim the account at trumpaccounts.gov or in the app, since the Treasury has been opening accounts on its own since October. Second, file IRS Form 4547 to request the $1,000 federal seed. No form means no deposit.

He also covers the fine print. Anyone can contribute up to $5,000 a year combined, and the $1,000 seed sits outside that cap. Employers can add up to $2,500, and Goldman Sachs, BlackRock and Nasdaq have said they will match the federal seed.
